area: mdl/executor + modelsdk/mpr (create or modify microflow, per statement)
symptom: `exec` of 200 `create or modify microflow` statements on a project of 5,373 units spent a third of its CPU in the garbage collector and allocated 2.2 GB, about 11 MB per statement (mendixlabs/mxcli#1842, ako/mxcli#2160).
cause: Three things rebuilt per statement from every unit of the project: (1) mprread.ListUnitsNamed listed the header of every microflow to keep the one with the name, several times per statement -- 45% of all bytes allocated; (2) the name-clash check listed every microflow header again to match one name; (3) modifyFlowInPlace discarded the container hierarchy after every statement, so the next one listed every unit to rebuild it, though an edit in place changes no container.
file: modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go (ListUnitHeadersWhere), modelsdk/mprread/generic.go (ListUnitsNamed, ListUnitHeadersWhere), mdl/backend/modelsdk/microflow.go (ListMicroflowHeadersWhere), mdl/executor/validate_name_clash.go (microflowHeadersNamedFold), mdl/executor/cmd_flow_modify.go
fix: Filter on the name inside the header listing; look the name-clash target up through the same filter; keep the hierarchy unless the statement moved the flow. 2.99 s -> 2.20 s for the 200 statements, written files byte-identical.
insight: A CPU profile showed the cost as 'GC 39%' and pointed nowhere. The allocation profile (pprof allocs, alloc_space, -cum) named the three call sites in one run: when the collector is the top entry, profile bytes allocated, not time. mxcli has no switch for it; a scratch build wrote pprof.Lookup("allocs") beside the CPU profile.
test: modelsdk/mpr/reader_unit_headers_where_test.go (the filtered listing is the listing filtered, for filters that divide it), mdl/executor/hierarchy_kept_pedapp_test.go (same hierarchy across two edits in place, a new one after a move, and the moved flow described correctly), mdl/executor/named_name_set_pedapp_test.go. Mutations of each fail, except that never discarding on a move is still caught by the folder move's own invalidation.
